title: Novartis delpacibart braxlosiran (del-brax) Phase I/II study in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) meets primary biomarker endpoint
body_text: Ad hoc announcement pursuant to Art. 53 LR FORTITUDE study met primary and key secondary endpoints of reduction in KHDC1L and creatine kinase levels, with safety profile consistent with previous results Del-brax indicates potential to become the first disease-modifying treatment for FSHD, a progressive and irreversible neuromuscular disease affecting approximately 45-87k people in the US and EU Novartis plans to engage global regulatory authorities on Phase I/II data; Phase III study currently enrolling Basel, June 11, 2026 – Novartis announced today that the biomarker cohort of the FORTITUDE Phase I/II study of del-brax met its primary and key secondary endpoints, with reductions in KHDC1L (cDUX) and creatine kinase biomarker levels indicating both strong target engagement and reduction in muscle damage in patients with facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). Del-brax is an investigational antibody oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) – a new class of RNA therapeutics – showing potential to become the first disease-modifying treatment for FSHD, a rare, irreversible neuromuscular disease marked by relentless loss of muscle function and progressive disability. “The FORTITUDE biomarker cohort data importantly replicate the target engagement and downstream muscle protection seen with del-brax in earlier dose-escalation cohorts. These results validate the dosing regimen implemented in our Phase III trial and lend further evidence of the potential for del-brax to have a significant impact for people with FSHD,” said Nazem Atassi, Global Head, Neuroscience and Gene Therapy Development, Novartis. “We are now evaluating the totality of the biomarker and clinical data and look forward to discussions with global regulatory agencies as we work with urgency to advance the development of del-brax for patients in need.” Del-brax is designed to address the root cause of FSHD, the aberrant expression of DUX4. Combining the tissue specificity of monoclonal antibodies with the precision of oligonucleotides, the AOC platform enables targeted delivery of siRNA to suppress DUX4 expression in previously hard-to-reach muscle cells of FSHD patients. Del-brax is the only investigational agent showing disease-modifying potential for FSHD in clinical studies. This investigational therapy has received FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations, and EMA Orphan Drug designation, and is currently in Phase III development. Del-brax is one of three potential first-in-class, late-stage, disease-modifying AOC therapies added to the Novartis neuroscience pipeline through the acquisition of Avidity Biosciences completed in February 2026. Beyond del-brax for FSHD, the Avidity acquisition included delpacibart-etedesiran (del-desiran) in Phase III development for myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1), a rare progressive neuromuscular disorder with a poor prognosis and no disease-modifying therapies; and delpacibart-zotadirsen (del-zota) in Phase II development for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), a severe, early-onset disease marked by progressive muscle damage and reduced life expectancy. Together, these programs build on Novartis’ expertise in spinal muscular atrophy, creating an industry-leading neuromuscular pipeline. About the del-brax FORTITUDE clinical development program The FORTITUDE Phase I/II study ( NCT05747924 ) is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and exploratory efficacy of del-brax in 90 patients with FSHD. The Phase I/II trial has three dose cohorts. The first two dose escalation cohorts A & B evaluated del-brax 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg versus placebo and were designed to assess safety as well as inform the dose and dose regimen of del-brax. Topline results from these two initial cohorts were presented at the 32ⁿᵈ FSHD International Research Congress in June 2025. Based on these results, the del-brax 2 mg/kg dose every 6 weeks was selected for Cohort C and the Phase III study. Cohort C, a biomarker cohort, assessed the impact of del-brax 2 mg/kg every 6 weeks versus placebo for 12 months in 51 FSHD patients aged 16-70. The primary endpoint of the study cohort was change in plasma concentration of KHDC1L, a DUX4-regulated circulating biomarker. The key secondary endpoint was change from baseline in the levels of creatine kinase, a marker of muscle damage. FORTITUDE-3 ( NCT07038200 ), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III study evaluating the efficacy and safety of del-brax, is currently enrolling 200 patients with FSHD aged 16-70 years. The primary endpoint is quantitative muscle testing (QMT) in the US and the 10-meter walk/run test (10MWRT) in Europe. Secondary endpoints include additional clinical functional measures, patient-reported outcomes on signs and symptoms of FSHD, and biomarkers. About FSHD Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is one of the most common forms of muscular dystrophy and is caused by aberrant expression of the DUX4 gene. The rare neuromuscular disease is estimated to affect between 45,000 to 87,000 people in the US and EU. People with FSHD typically begin to experience symptoms in their teenage or early adult years, characterized by progressive muscle weakness, pain, fatigue and disability. The disease leads to a steady loss of independence, with 20% of patients becoming wheelchair dependent. There are no currently approved therapies for FSHD. Novartis in neuroscience Neurological diseases are deeply personal, affecting people of any age, from newborns to seniors, often striking in the prime of life. At Novartis, we are doubling down on our commitment to neurology, expanding our legacy of innovation in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and multiple sclerosis (MS) to work in neuroimmunology, neurodegeneration, and neuromuscular diseases. Our goal is to protect people’s health across their lifespan, developing more treatment options that lead to better outcomes. title: What are backlinks in SEO & how do I get them?
summary: Backlinks signal trust and authority to search engines and AI. Learn 7 proven ways to build them.
body_text: Backlinks are one of the most important signals search engines and AI systems use to decide which sites deserve visibility. This guide breaks down what backlinks are, why they matter across both organic and AI search, the factors that affect their value, and proven ways to build them. Backlinks are a credibility record, not just a ranking signal Every time another reputable website links to yours, it's casting a vote of confidence in your content. Over time, those votes accumulate into something more significant than a ranking factor. They form a credibility record that both search engines and AI systems draw on when deciding what to surface. Search engines like Google have used this record for decades. But AI search tools (including AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity) are now drawing on it, too. When AI search systems generate responses and decide which sources to cite, they're leaning heavily on the same signals of authority and trustworthiness that search engines have always valued. That means sites with strong backlink profiles are ranking well on Google and being cited in AI-generated answers. Think of your backlink profile as one record with two evaluators. Your backlink profile doesn't change depending on who's evaluating it. A link from a respected industry publication carries weight, whether it's a search engine crawler following it or an AI system assessing your site's credibility. Both are asking the same underlying question: “Is this a source worth sending people to?” If backlinks were purely a ranking mechanism, their value would fluctuate every time an algorithm update changed how they're weighted. But as a credibility record, they're more durable (and more broadly useful) than that. What are backlinks? Backlinks are links from other websites pointing to yours that signal trust and authority to improve your visibility in search engine results and AI-generated answers. Plus, backlinks can also drive referral traffic directly from those linking sites to yours. From the perspective of the site linking out, these are called external links, outbound links, or outgoing links. But when other sites link to your website, they become your backlinks. You can acquire backlinks naturally when other sites discover and link to your content. Or you can proactively build them through outreach and by cultivating relationships. To quickly see your site's backlinks (or any competitor's backlinks), use our free Backlink Checker . Types of backlinks Not all backlinks are the same. Here are the main types and what each signals to your credibility record: Editorial backlinks : Links that are earned naturally when a site links to your content as a trusted source. These provide the strongest credibility signal. Guest post backlinks : Links that are placed within content you've written for another site. These signal relevance and expertise when the host site is topically aligned with your site. Business profile and directory backlinks : Links from listings, associations, or partner pages. These signal legitimacy and local or industry presence. UGC and sponsored backlinks : Links in user-generated content (e.g., forums and comments) or paid placements, typically marked nofollow. These were historically treated as lower-credibility signals, though Google has acknowledged that nofollow is just a hint, so these can still contribute to visibility. Social backlinks : Links from social media platforms. While they might not carry much direct SEO value, they drive traffic and put your content in front of audiences who may link to it from their own sites. For a deeper breakdown, see our guide to the different types of backlinks . Why backlinks matter for search engine and AI visibility Backlinks matter in SEO and AI SEO because they signal that your content is reputable and that your website is authoritative. The backlinks you acquire are a powerful signal that search engines and AI systems use to evaluate whether a site deserves visibility, but they work slightly differently across each. In organic search, Google uses backlinks as a core input to its PageRank algorithm. PageRank can be thought of as a measure of page authority. And pages pass authority (also known as link equity) to each other through links. The higher a page’s PageRank, the more equity it can pass to the pages it links to. Pages with strong backlink profiles pass more equity to the pages they link to. That boosts authority across your site without diminishing the authority of those already reputable pages. You can see the impact of strong backlink profiles on competitive queries. For instance, the top-ranking pages for "iphone reviews" have hundreds of backlinks: And the corresponding domains have millions of backlinks: In AI search, the relationship between backlinks and performance is equally significant. A Semrush study of 1,000 domains found that high-quality backlinks meaningfully improve AI visibility. And considering Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode are built on top of existing search infrastructure, backlinks likely play a large role in whether your content gets surfaced in Google’s AI search experiences. Just be aware that Google's link spam policies exist to discourage manipulative link building. Violating them risks a Google penalty that can hurt your visibility across both organic search and AI experiences. What affects the value of a backlink in SEO? Some backlinks are more beneficial for SEO than others, some have the potential to harm your visibility, and some probably have no impact. Let’s explore the main factors that affect the value of a backlink in SEO: Follow status When a backlink has a nofollow attribute indicating the publisher doesn’t want the link to be seen as an endorsement, the link can be less valuable for improving search visibility. Publishers can suggest that search systems don’t follow a link by adding one of these attributes to the link’s HTML: rel=“nofollow”: The linking site doesn’t want to endorse the target site rel=“sponsored”: The target site paid for the link to be placed on the linking site rel=“ugc”: The link appears within user-generated content (like forum comments) Adding one of these attributes creates a nofollow link . Like this: Click here “Follow” links (sometimes called “dofollow” links) don’t contain any of the above attributes. Google is more likely to follow these, though there's no guarantee those links will positively affect your rankings. Google has also said that even nofollow links can serve as hints for ranking purposes. And our study on 1,000 domains found that nofollow links have nearly the same impact on AI visibility as follow links. This supports the idea that AI systems read your backlink profile as a whole. The holistic record matters more than any single attribute on individual links. To check whether your backlinks are marked as nofollow, use Semrush’s Backlinks tool. If you find a link that’s marked nofollow, consider reaching out to the relevant contact and asking them to change it to a follow link. Domain and page authority The more authoritative the domain and page linking to your website, the more valuable that backlink can be. For instance, a link from the World Health Organization carries more weight than one from a small, unknown health blog for search engines and AI systems alike. While Google and AI tools don't publish authority metrics, Semrush's Authority Score (AS) offers a useful approximation. AS measures domain and page authoritativeness based on: Link power : The quality and quantity of backlinks Organic traffic : Estimated monthly unpaid visits from search engines Natural profile : How natural (rather than spammy) the backlink profile appears It's also worth targeting sites that consistently publish well-researched, accurate, and helpful content. These sites are more likely to be perceived as authoritative based on engagement signals and brand mentions. Topical relevance Backlinks from websites and content that are relevant to yours carry more weight because they appear more natural to search engines and more trustworthy to AI systems. Healthline earning backlinks from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), for example, is more valuable than Healthline earning links from a similarly authoritative sports site. Plus, visitors who arrive via topically relevant backlinks are more likely to engage with your content and convert. Link placement and context Where a link appears on a page and how likely it is to be clicked may affect how much value it passes. Google's reasonable surfer model patent suggests links are weighted by click likelihood, factoring in: Placement : Links high in the main content are more likely to be clicked than footer links, for example Content quality : Higher-quality content and context make a click more likely Link density : Fewer links on a page means more attention and value per link Just bear in mind that we can’t say for certain whether Google actually uses this model in its algorithms. Anchor text Anchor text is the clickable text a link is attached to, and it helps search engines understand what the linked page is about. Some marketers try to build links with keyword-rich anchor text like "buy men's wedding shoes” and “wedding shoes for men online" to manipulate rankings. But unnatural anchor text is a form of link spam that can trigger a Google penalty. Instead, use descriptive, natural-sounding anchor text. And avoid building large numbers of links with identical anchor text. Link schemes Link schemes are attempts to manipulate rankings and SEO performance through unhelpful or spammy backlinks. Google identifies and ignores most link schemes. However, participating in link schemes at scale can lead to a penalty. Practices to avoid: Paying for follow links Participating in link exchanges (i.e., "link to me and I'll link to you") Using automated link building programs Getting links from low-quality directory sites Adding unnatural links in forum comments Creating content purely to generate backlinks If you've engaged in any of these practices, use Semrush's Backlink Audit tool to identify potentially toxic backlinks and remove them if necessary. From the " Audit " report, review flagged links and move harmful ones to the " Remove " tab. From there, you can email site owners directly to request removal. As a last resort, disavow toxic links (i.e., formally ask Google to ignore them). Only do this if you have a large volume of harmful links you can't remove and are at risk of (or have already received) a Google penalty. Disavowing incorrectly can hurt your site’s search visibility. 7 ways to build valuable backlinks for SEO Here are seven proven link building tactics to try: 1. Create useful resources Create useful resources that are hard for others to replicate or improve upon, so publishers have a good reason to cite your website in their content. For example, Healthline has an in-depth article about how much water you should drink. It’s cited as a source in many related articles, like this one from HuffPost: It’s crucial that the resources you create are highly relevant to your brand because: It makes your content more trustworthy and more likely to get linked to It means you’re more likely to attract links from topically relevant sites The content is more likely to generate other business benefits (like conversions from referral traffic) Original data, proprietary frameworks, and comprehensive guides are also among the types of assets AI systems most frequently cite in their generated answers. So, the same qualities that earn editorial backlinks tend to improve AI visibility. If you need inspiration, see which of your competitors’ pages attract the most backlinks by analyzing their domains in the Backlinks tool and going to the “Indexed Pages” report. High-quality content like this can attract backlinks naturally. But you can also use outreach tactics to build links . 2. Try broken link building Broken link building is the process of finding backlinks that don’t work (e.g., because the target page was deleted) and suggesting a relevant backlink to your website as a replacement. Broken link building works well because publishers don’t want broken links on their sites. And you’re offering them an easy solution that will improve their user experience. To find broken links, you can suggest alternatives to, look for links that were supposed to point to your site in the first place. Just go to the “ Indexed Pages ” report for your domain in the Backlinks tool and apply the “Broken Pages” filter. If you have a good replacement for any broken page you see here, click the corresponding number in the “Backlinks” column. Then, decide which broken backlinks are worth trying to recover (if any) based on the authority of the page, the context of the link, etc. Finally, email the relevant contact(s) to let them know about your broken backlink and your suggested replacement. Here’s an email template you can use: Subject line: Resource suggestion for [Page Title] Hi [Name], I was reading your article on [topic/page title] and noticed that the link to [describe the resource briefly] appears to be broken. Here's the specific link: [broken URL] I recently published a similar resource that covers [brief description of your content]. If you think it would be helpful for your readers, here it is: [your URL] Either way, I wanted to give you a heads up about the broken link. Best,[Your name] 3. Answer relevant media requests Finding and responding to relevant media requests can be an effective way to build website backlinks because creators often credit their contributors with a link. You can find media requests to respond to on websites like Help a Reporter Out (HARO), Qwoted , and Featured . Generally, you need to follow these steps when you want to use a platform to respond to media requests: Sign up to your chosen platform(s) and create a profile Opt in to alerts about relevant requests and monitor your email inbox Respond to relevant requests as quickly and helpfully as possible Responding to media requests requires time and patience, as you are essentially competing with other sources. To increase your success, lead with a specific, quotable insight. Journalists are on a deadline and need copy they can use immediately. Check out our guide to HARO link building to learn how to use this tactic effectively. 4. Run digital PR campaigns Digital PR is the practice of creating newsworthy content and distributing it to journalists and publishers to earn coverage and backlinks at scale. Unlike reactive media requests, most PR campaigns are proactive. You create the story, then pitch it. For example, in 2022, the marketing agency Yard published a report on which celebrities contributed the most to CO2 emissions from their private jet use. Since then, Yard’s study has earned roughly 2,800 links from over 1,100 different websites and publications. When your digital PR campaign is done right, your referring domains should skew more toward links from mass media, newspapers, and publishers. Effective digital PR assets tend to be: Original data : Surveys, studies, or proprietary datasets journalists can't get elsewhere Timely angles : Content tied to news cycles, seasonal trends, or cultural moments Visually compelling : Infographics or interactive content that's easy for publishers to embed You’ll need to research what stories different publications are focusing on and align your angle to match. You can also use services like Pitchbox and Muckrack to widely distribute your content and allow journalists to organically pick up your story to share. The goal is to earn some links and brand placements in major publications because they carry outsized weight for your search and AI visibility. A single high-authority citation can improve your chances of appearing in AI-generated answers more than dozens of low-authority links. 5. Guest post on relevant sites Guest posting content on other sites in your niche helps you earn topically relevant backlinks and build a consistent presence across credible publications that AI systems use as a trust signal. Focus on sites that publish well-researched content in your space, have a real audience, and where a link back to your site would make contextual sense. Avoid sites that exist purely to host guest posts. These carry minimal credibility and can look manipulative to search engines. Before pitching, check the target site's Authority Score and backlink profile in the Backlinks tool. If their profile looks thin or spammy, move on. When pitching, lead with a specific article idea rather than a general offer to write. Editors respond better to a concrete, relevant angle they can say yes or no to. 6. Replicate your competitors’ backlinks Replicating competitor backlinks can be a highly effective tactic because it means using methods that have already worked. To get started, add your domain and up to four rival domains to the Backlink Gap tool. You’ll see the “Best” link building prospects by default. These are domains that link to all analyzed competitors but not to you. Click the arrows in the corresponding rows and columns to learn more about your competitors’ backlinks. And determine if those links are possible (and worthwhile) to replicate. For example, if your competitor has a backlink because their CEO gave an interview to the site, you might want to contact the publisher to see if they’re interested in interviewing your CEO, too. 7. Capitalize on business relationships Use your existing business relationships to try to get backlinks placed on your partners’ websites. For example, you can get backlinks through existing relationships by: Supplying case studies to service providers Providing testimonials to freelancers Getting featured as a preferred vendor on distributors' websites Announcing joint projects on partners' blogs Getting listed on trade association websites To get started, list all the website owners that your business has an affiliation with. Then, explore their sites to look for link building opportunities. Once you have an idea, consider who at your business has the strongest relationship with the partner. Ask them to review the idea and propose it to their contact. Track your link building work and brand credibility Building backlinks is an ongoing process, and monitoring your credibility record over time is just as important as the outreach itself. Semrush's Brand Monitoring app lets you track both backlinks and unlinked mentions in one place. Unlinked mentions are worth paying attention to because search engines and AI systems pick up on brand signals across the web. A consistent mention pattern from credible sources reinforces your authority even without a link, and they're easy outreach targets to convert into one. Try the Brand Monitoring app today. Share Cecilia Meis Cecilia is a senior editor and strategist with more than 12 years of experience shaping editorial strategies, refining brand messaging, and leading high-impact teams. She began her career in print and digital editorial leadership roles before transitioning to SEO and digital marketing, focusing on data-driven strategies. She‘s passionate about ensuring operational efficiency, upholding editorial standards, and mentoring writers to deliver top-quality, brand-aligned content.

title: Oceania Cruises® Spotlights Its Signature Wellness Discovery Tours
body_text: Luxury Travelers Embrace the Rejuvenating Power of Travel Through Wellness Experiences Rooted in Local Traditions Oceania Vista® sailing in Santorini, Greece, and yoga and stretch classes aboard Oceania Cruises' ships. Download high-resolution images here . (Credit: Oceania Cruises®) MIAMI , July 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- From practicing tai chi in Bangkok, to dance therapy in Colombo, to yoga and wine tasting in Santorini, Oceania Cruises ®, the world's leading destination- and culinary-focused luxury cruise line, invites discerning travelers to embrace a new era of exploration through its acclaimed Wellness Discovery Tours. Responding to a growing interest in wellness experiences, Oceania Cruises offers more than 50 Wellness Discovery Tours in destinations throughout Asia, Europe and South America, as luxury travelers are increasingly seeking journeys that allow them to learn new skills and explore the world differently. This signature collection of tours offers opportunities to engage with centuries-old healing traditions, mindfulness practices and local cultures across the globe. "Travel has become one of the most powerful ways people invest in their wellbeing. It's a means of stepping outside of their usual routine to slow down, explore different cultures and destinations, and return home with a renewed perspective," said Jason Montague, Chief Luxury Officer of Oceania Cruises. "Our Wellness Discovery Tours are designed for those seeking to nurture their wellbeing and discover the rejuvenating power of travel. For today's luxury guest, travel is much more than movement from place to place – it is a journey of discovery, with every voyage offering the chance to expand horizons, deepen understanding and return home transformed by new perspectives." Intended to inspire connection and enrichment, Oceania Cruises' small-group, wellness-oriented tours bring guests together with local specialists and like-minded travelers. Experiences range from mineral-rich baths and yoga to dance, power walking and culinary classes. These shoreside encounters are complemented by a wealth of enriching experiences on board Oceania Cruises' intimate, luxurious ships. With culinary lectures, hands-on cooking classes and food and beverage pairing experiences, plus creative workshops in the Artist Loft, insightful guest speakers and performances by local musicians, guests can enjoy a diverse program designed to enhance their journey. The enrichment options both ashore and on board are encompassed by the serenity of the adults-only environment aboard Oceania Cruises' boutique ships, allowing guests to explore an extraordinary array of destinations at their own pace and with like-minded travelers. Highlights of Oceania Cruises Wellness Discovery Tours : Ultimate Traditional Dance Therapy – Colombo, Sri Lanka: Release tension and lift your mood through Kandyan dance, learning the moves and rituals of Sri Lanka's national dance in an uplifting group setting. Saigonese Organic Food Tasting – Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: Savor organic teas and vegetarian cuisine, engaging with local experts and gaining insights into Vietnam's celebrated tea culture. Tai Chi at Viharn Sien Park – Bangkok, Thailand: Visit a serene urban park in the shadow of the temple Viharn Sien to practice the slow, fluid movements of tai chi, an ancient form of exercise improving strength, flexibility and balance. Healthy Stroll Along the Cliffs and Getxo – Bilbao, Spain: Traverse geologically rich cliff paths, pass 18th-century windmills and fortresses, and experience the Basque fishing village of Getxo – with time to enjoy local tapas and authentic culture. Thermal Baths of the Popes – Rome (Civitavecchia), Italy: Restore mind and body at Terme dei Papi, soaking in mineral-rich waters beloved by popes, artists and poets for centuries, set in the inspirational Italian countryside. Traditional Chinese Medicine Experience – Hong Kong, China: Consult with a traditional medicine doctor and try therapies such as acupuncture or cupping, learning ancient methods to promote relaxation and vitality. Yoga & Wine Tasting Overlooking Caldera – Santorini, Greece: Find tranquility with a meditative yoga session on a winery terrace, followed by tastings of Santorini's distinct vintages while admiring the breathtaking views. Tai Chi & Vegetarian Lunch at a Monastery – Hanoi, Vietnam: Experience mindful movement surrounded by spectacular natural beauty and spiritual heritage in a Buddhist monastery on Yen Tu Mountain. Volcanic Thermal Pools and Naples – Naples/Pompeii, Italy: Alternate between hot and cold pools, surrounded by ancient landscapes and timeless healing traditions. Patagonian Hot Springs & Fjord Cruise – Puerto Chacabuco, Chile: Invite relaxation and mindfulness with a journey through the Aysén Fjord by catamaran to the secluded Ensenada Perez Hot Springs, where Patagonian landscapes surround naturally heated pools. Oceania Cruises is celebrated for its personalized service, award-winning cuisine and a crew-to-guest ratio designed for exceptional comfort. With destination-intensive itineraries ranging from seven to 180 days, guests return home with renewed energy, inspiration and stories that last a lifetime. For more information visit OceaniaCruises.com or call 855-OCEANIA. About Oceania Cruises® Oceania Cruises® is the world's leading destination- and culinary-focused luxury cruise line, celebrated for its port-rich voyages and authentic cultural and culinary experiences. The line's intimate, luxurious ships feature an adults-only environment, with a high proportion of spacious rooms and suites, calling on more than 600 marquee and boutique ports in more than 100 countries across seven continents, with destination-intensive itineraries ranging from seven to 180 days. Aboard the designer-inspired ships, guests enjoy personalized service supported by a strong crew-to-guest ratio, alongside The Finest Cuisine at Sea®, prepared by one of the highest chef-to-guest ratios at sea. Oceania Cruises® is also recognized as one of the world's most awarded cruise lines, with accolades spanning luxury, dining, service and destination experiences. Oceania Cruises® has five Sonata Class ships on order scheduled for delivery in 2027, 2029, 2032, 2035 and 2037. Oceania Cruises® is a wholly owned subsidiary of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. (NYSE: NCLH). title: A color change. A precipitation. A smell nobody expected. The most important observations in chemistry are often the ones no sensor captures.
summary: Read the latest news and updates from ReactWise about AI-driven chemistry and process optimization.
body_text: A color change. A precipitation. A smell nobody expected. The most important observations in chemistry are often the ones no sensor captures. I still remember a late-night reaction run during my master’s where everything looked right on paper - temperature stable, reagents added correctly, timing on schedule. But the mixture had turned a shade darker than expected. Just enough to make me pause. No instrument flagged it. But every chemist who has spent some time at the bench knows that feeling. Something is off, and you can't yet explain why. That color change turned out to be the first sign of an unwanted decomposition reaction. This is what makes chemistry uniquely hard to digitize, and honestly, the most interesting science to build software for. Phase separation, color, texture - these carry real chemical information that doesn't fit neatly into a database column. And the knowledge of an experienced chemist is largely procedural - it lives in how they do something, not just what they know. Free text observations sometimes matter more than most data systems acknowledge. "Mixture turned slightly yellow upon addition" carries real scientific meaning that no category or number captures. This is exactly where Vera - @ReactWise's AI assistant - comes in: reasoning across unstructured observations, connecting them to patterns across historical campaigns, and surfacing what might otherwise be missed. AI can spot patterns no single human could hold simultaneously. But when something truly unexpected happens, the decision to intervene will always need a human. AI can support that judgment. It cannot own it. The goal was never to abstract chemistry away. It was to make the chemist who understands all of that even more powerful. ‍

So when their hair begins to shed, it can feel like progress in one area has brought a new worry somewhere else. Can GLP-1 medications cause hair loss? Or is the shedding connected to the body changes that can happen during treatment? In many cases, hair shedding during a GLP-1 routine may be related to weight change, appetite shifts, nutrition gaps, and physical stress on the body rather than direct follicle injury. When the body changes quickly, more hairs can move into the resting phase, creating a temporary shedding condition called telogen effluvium. The good news is that resting hair follicles are not permanently damaged follicles. GLP-1-related hair shedding can feel sudden, but the hair cycle can recover as weight change slows, nutrition becomes more consistent, and the scalp gets steady care. When the body is adapting to fast change, the hair cycle can become more sensitive. GLP-1 medications can influence appetite, digestion, and blood sugar regulation. That can mean smaller portions, fewer snacks, less interest in food, or skipped meals. Those changes may support weight-management plans, while also making hair-supporting nutrition harder to maintain. Faster Weight Loss Can Send a Stress Signal to the Hair Cycle A smaller appetite can mean less protein. Fewer meals can mean fewer chances to get iron, zinc, vitamin D, B vitamins, and healthy fats. Faster weight loss can also act like a larger adjustment signal to the body. The body may temporarily prioritize essential functions over hair growth during a major transition. GLP-1 Hair Shedding Usually Looks Diffuse GLP-1 hair shedding usually looks diffuse. Your part, crown, temples, or ponytail may look thinner, even if your hairline has not sharply receded. Washing your hair does not cause this shedding. It often reveals hairs that were already ready to release. Shedding may also feel more noticeable when weight loss is faster or when other triggers overlap. These can include: Low protein intake Low ferritin or iron concerns Low vitamin D or B12 Thyroid changes Postpartum changes Menopause High stress Recent illness Surgery Restrictive dieting Tight hairstyles Existing female pattern hair thinning Patchy, Painful, or Scarring Hair Loss Needs Medical Attention: Diffuse stress shedding is often temporary. Resting follicles are usually not permanently damaged follicles. Still, patchy hair loss, burning, scaling, sores, shiny scarring areas, eyebrow loss, or painful scalp symptoms should be checked by a dermatologist. Those signs may point to a different type of hair loss that deserves a closer look. If your portions are smaller or meals are easier to skip, your hair may be getting fewer building blocks than it needs during an already demanding season of body change. Start with protein. Hair is made largely from keratin, so steady protein intake helps support the next growth cycle. When you feel full quickly, eating protein earlier in the meal can help you get more from smaller portions. Helpful options include: Eggs Greek yogurt Fish Poultry Tofu Lentils Beans Protein smoothies Cottage cheese After protein, look at nutrients that help support healthy hair and scalp function. Protein, iron, zinc, biotin, vitamin D, B12, and healthy fats may be worth discussing with a clinician depending on your diet, symptoms, and lab results. If shedding feels heavy, lasts longer than expected, or comes with fatigue, dizziness, restrictive eating, or heavy menstrual bleeding, ask your clinician whether lab testing makes sense. Supplements can be useful when there is a real gap, but more is not always better. High-dose iron, vitamin D, zinc, B12, or biotin may not be right for everyone. The smartest hair-support plan starts with what you are eating, what symptoms you are noticing, and what your labs show. Nutrition supports the internal side of recovery. Your scalp and strands also need a routine that feels steady, gentle, and easy to repeat. Why Quick Fixes Do Not Work for GLP-1 Hair Shedding It is completely understandable to want an overnight fix when you are seeing more hair in the shower or noticing a wider part. But telogen effluvium does not work like a switch. Once more follicles have moved into the resting phase, those hairs may shed even after your body is already starting to stabilize. Rather than trying to force every strand to stay, focus on supporting the next growth cycle with steady, gentle care. Start with the basics this week: Keep taking your medication as prescribed unless your clinician tells you otherwise. Eat protein early in the day, especially if your appetite is low. Avoid repeated skipped meals when possible. Ask about lab testing if shedding feels heavy or comes with fatigue. Use gentle scalp care instead of harsh scrubbing or product hopping. Avoid tight ponytails, buns, extensions, and aggressive brushing. Track shedding for two to four weeks. See a dermatologist if hair loss is patchy, painful, scarring, or persistent. Hair recovery takes time, but that does not mean you are helpless while you wait. Consistent nutrition, scalp support, and medical guidance can help create better conditions for healthier-looking regrowth. GLP-1 Hair Loss: What Women Should Know Women may report or notice GLP-1-related hair shedding more often because part-line density, ponytail thickness, hormones, iron status, and existing shedding can all affect how visible hair changes become. For many women, the first sign is not a bald spot. It is a wider-looking part, a thinner ponytail, more scalp showing at the crown, or extra shedding around the temples and hairline. You may notice the change before anyone else does, and that concern is valid. Shedding during a GLP-1 routine can also overlap with other hair triggers. Telogen effluvium can increase shedding for a few months, while female pattern hair thinning can slowly affect density over time. Iron levels, thyroid changes, postpartum changes, menopause, stress, restrictive eating, and heavy periods can also influence the hair cycle. For many people, the most likely type of shedding is telogen effluvium, a temporary response that can happen after physical stress or major body change. Is hair loss a side effect of GLP-1 medications? title: What Is Emotional Advertising and How To Effectively Use It?
summary: Emotional marketing aims to use pathos to get people to purchase a good or service. Learn more about how to use emotional marketing today.
body_text: Emotional advertising lets you use emotions to encourage customers to purchase your products. One way to approach emotional marketing is via the rhetorical triangle . This triangle’s three sides are the speaker (ethos), audience (pathos), and message (logos). Your advertising strategy will include all three of these elements, and emotional advertising lets you create a message that connects with your audience. You can also learn to understand emotional marketing without the rhetorical triangle. This guide will help you understand what emotion in advertising is, why it is important, and showcase some emotional marketing examples for inspiration. What is emotional advertising? Emotional marketing refers to when your message uses human emotion to connect deeper with your audience. It is very common for emotional marketing to just appeal to one emotion, such as joy, anger, or fear. However, it can appeal to multiple emotions, and you can technically use any emotion you want. How does emotional appeal advertising work? While most of the above examples of emotional marketing are for major international brands, it works just as well for small businesses . In fact, many small businesses may do even better with emotional marketing because they are more likely to have a closer relationship with clients already. You can take advantage of a few trends in emotional marketing to get the results you want for your small business. You’ll notice that these cover all of the basic emotions, with each type of emotional response leading to a different result. That being said, any strong emotional reactions can lead to the positive results you want. Remember that SMS marketing is among the most effective ways to spread your message, thanks to its 98% open rate and customers’ general preference for businesses contacting them over text than in any other way. Sadness = More Clicks When we experience feelings of sadness, this can generate more clicks. This comes from the fact that sadness leads to connections and empathy. Importantly, empathy leads to the motivation to help others and altruism. This is why the ASPCA’s ads use sad photos and music to encourage donations. Although your business probably doesn’t need donations, the use of sadness still translates into clicks. It is the way that people can give back after feeling these emotions. Anger/Disgust = Viral Content When people feel anger or disgust, they tend to vent about it, which leads to content going viral. So, you should consider incorporating anger and related human emotions into advertising when you want to take advantage of viral marketing. This connection between eliciting anxiety and anger and increasing your content’s spread or viral nature has even been confirmed in research . Happiness = More Shares If you want to encourage more shares of your content, then focus on happiness. Research shows that positive content and good news travels more quickly on social media. Harness this to get more shares for your content and advertising. This is also related to the idea of the “social smile.” This refers specifically to babies smiling when others smile, but it also applies to adults. In adults, it is the fact that happiness tends to spread, so if someone else feels happy, you tend to feel happy as well. This, in turn, encourages sharing of the content that made you smile. Companies can take advantage of this by including happy customers in their marketing. Fear/Surprises = Loyalty When people experience fear or surprise, they want to stick to familiar and comfortable things. Using those emotions in your advertising encourages people to stick to your brand, as it is familiar. That leads to brand loyalty. Many marketers feel hesitant to use the emotion of fear, as you don’t want negative feelings associated with your brand. But when done right, you can make your business seem like one of the few good things in the scary or surprising world. 4 Benefits of Emotional Appeal in Advertising Emotional appeal advertising can play a key role in marketing for several reasons, including the following. Emotions make your product more memorable. When you play on emotions, you will get the advantage of your advertising being more memorable. Research shows that people are more likely to have long-lasting memories of emotionally charged events. This translates into marketing as well. Simply put, by creating advertising that has an emotional impact on your audience, it is much more likely that your content and, therefore, your brand will stay in their heads. Emotions forge connections. When you trigger emotions in your audience, you help form connections with them. This, in turn, leads to customer loyalty and a likely increase in brand advocates . In fact, one study found customers who emotionally connect with a brand have a lifetime value that’s 306% higher . The same study found that 71% of customers with an emotional connection are likely to recommend the company. By contrast, the average rate of people likely to recommend a given company is just 45%. Emotional content is more shareable. No matter the type of emotions you convey in your emotional commercials, ads, or other marketing content, this strategy makes your advertising highly shareable. That is because people love sharing content that makes them feel something. This applies to both positive and negative emotions. It can deliver better results. One study even found that emotional appeal ads were more effective than those with more rational content. That study found success rates of 31% and 16% , respectively. In other words, an emotional message almost doubled the success rate when compared to only rational content. 5 Tips to Create Ads That Appeal to Emotion To help you create successful ads that appeal to emotion, follow these five tips: 1. Know Your Audience The first step in creating emotional appeal in advertising is understanding who you’re talking to. Get to know your audience’s needs and desires. What are the pain points? When you have a clear picture of your target demographic, you can then tailor your message to resonate with them on a deeper level. 2. Tell Stories Humans are wired to connect with stories, and a well-crafted narrative can evoke those powerful emotions. Rather than just highlighting a product’s features, frame your ad within a story that illustrates how your product or service makes someone’s life better. 3. Be Authentic Consumers today crave authenticity. They’re tired of feeling like they’re being sold to in a way that feels inauthentic or manipulative. Instead, focus on being real. Whether it’s showing the behind-the-scenes of your business or sharing testimonials from genuine customers, authenticity builds trust. 4. Use User-Generated Content User-generated content (UGC) is a great way to tap into genuine emotion. When real customers share their stories, experiences, photos, or videos with your product, it builds social proof and creates a sense of community. UGC not only makes your brand feel more relatable, but it also taps into the trust and emotional connection people have with other real people, not just brands. 5. Create Visual Impact Images, colors, music—these are all things that evoke emotion. A well-designed ad doesn’t just communicate; it feels. Pair your imagery with music that complements the mood, and watch how your audience becomes emotionally invested in the message you’re trying to convey. Emotions are often triggered by what people see and hear, so use this to your advantage. 6 Emotional Advertising Examples of Brands That Did it Right To get you started on your journey to using emotional marketing, seek out some emotional appeal advertising examples, specifically looking at brands that did an excellent job with it. Some also use tips you will find in our attraction marketing guide . The following are mostly more prominent brands, but all of their emotional appeal strategies work just as well, if not better, for small, local businesses. Consider looking at the following marketing efforts to get inspiration for your content marketing strategy. Youth — Spartan Spartan, a tough racing community, shows that your brand doesn’t need to be a household name to take advantage of emotional advertising. It plays on the idea that everyone is young at heart and that anyone can do this activity. The ad features videos of people completing the challenging races and obstacle courses, and it highlights people of all ages, sizes, and ethnicities. The ad also strongly plays on the emotion of happiness, as nearly everyone in the video is smiling. Pride — Code Salon In 2021, Code Salon played on emotions and connected with the public during Pride Month via a series of Facebook posts. The series of posts featured LGBTQ+ employees and staff, each of whom shared “what makes them proud.” This plays into happiness and the feeling of connecting with the community. Customers feel happy when seeing this content, so positive impressions form around the brand. Love — Wren In 2014, Wren, a clothing brand, showed how emotional marketing can go viral. Its “first kiss” video showed two strangers kissing and led to a boost in sales of almost 14,000% . Its success comes from the intense emotions in the video and the fact that the brand was only mentioned subtly. Gratitude — P&G P&G offers a great example of emotional marketing in its “Thank You, Mom” ad from before the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi. This ad plays on the emotional connections of moms and their children. It features Olympians and highlights how their moms supported them to get where they are. This plays into the emotions of one of P&G’s target audience groups, moms, making them feel particularly valued by the company. Protection — Lysol Another example of emotional marketing that plays on the emotions of a mother comes from Lysol. Their ad “Protect Like a Mother” features a mom standing in front of dangerous animals, indicating she protects her children from them. This example aims to empower mothers while also building trust in the brand. Innovation — Apple Apple’s “Think Different” campaign was so successful that it earned the 1998 Emmy for Best Commercial. Apple used the slogan between 1997 and 2002. This campaign played on the satisfaction of changing the status quo and innovating. Enhance Your Emotional Marketing Strategy with AI Emotional appeal advertising is successful because people tend to have stronger memories of events connected with strong emotions. Emotional content is also highly shareable, as shown by the viral examples of good emotional advertising mentioned above. Local businesses can harness the power of emotions across their advertising campaigns, from SMS to digital advertisements to social media posts—all with the power of AI . Develop emotional marketing strategies that create positive feelings in your target audience, and you’ll notice an increase in sales and engagement thanks to those emotional responses. With Podium’s AI Employee , creating emotional appeal in advertising campaigns is easy. The solution analyzes customer sentiment and crafts personalized messages that resonate on a deeper level. Whether you’re looking to trigger nostalgia, joy, empathy, or excitement, Podium can match your messaging and tone, ensuring your campaigns connect on a deeper, more impactful level. title: How to Calculate the Real ROI of Multifamily AI and Win Budget Approval from Your Ownership Group
summary: Learn how to calculate multifamily AI ROI, identify the right metrics, and build a business case that wins budget approval from your ownership group.
body_text: How to Calculate the Real ROI of Multifamily AI and Win Budget Approval from Your Ownership Group Every ownership group meeting eventually arrives at the same question: "What's the return on this investment?" When the investment in question is AI, that question carries extra weight. AI in multifamily property management is no longer a futuristic concept, it's a live operational tool that competitors are already deploying. But enthusiasm alone does not unlock capital. A disciplined, data-backed multifamily AI ROI business case does. This guide walks asset managers, directors of operations, and multifamily leaders through the exact framework needed to quantify AI's impact, translate it into language ownership groups trust, and secure budget approval. Why Ownership Groups Push Back on AI Investment Before building your case, it helps to understand why skepticism exists. Ownership groups are not anti-technology, they are pro-return. Their hesitation around AI typically falls into three categories: Unclear cost boundaries. Licensing fees, implementation costs, training time, and integration expenses can be hard to pin down upfront. Vague benefit claims. Vendor promises like "increased efficiency" and "improved resident experience" are difficult to convert into dollar figures. Perceived risk. Ownership groups worry about disruption to operations, staff turnover driven by change, and the possibility that the technology underdelivers. A strong multifamily AI ROI business case addresses each of these concerns directly with specifics. How to Calculate ROI for AI in Multifamily Property Management The core formula for AI ROI in multifamily property management is: ROI (%) = [(Total Annual Value Generated − Total Annual Cost of AI) / Total Annual Cost of AI] × 100 To apply this formula meaningfully, you need to define both sides of the equation with precision. The sections below break down exactly how to do that across the key value drivers AI touches in a multifamily operation. Step 1: Establish Your Total Cost of AI Ownership Before you can show return, you need a clear picture of investment. The total cost of AI ownership in multifamily typically includes two categories. Direct Costs Software licensing or subscription fees (monthly or annual), implementation and onboarding fees, data integration or API connection costs, and ongoing platform support or success management fees. Indirect Costs Staff time spent on implementation and training, temporary productivity dip during the transition period, and any third-party consulting required for setup. Pull quotes from your vendor that itemize each of these. Ask specifically about pricing tiers relative to your unit count and whether costs scale with usage or remain flat. A realistic Year 1 cost estimate is essential and it will often look higher than Year 2 and beyond once one-time implementation costs are excluded. Pro tip: Build your business case using a three-year projection. Year 1 ROI may be modest given setup costs. Year 2 and Year 3 ROI figures tend to be significantly stronger, and ownership groups who think in asset-hold timelines will appreciate that lens. Step 2: Quantify the Revenue-Side Impact AI in leasing and revenue management directly influences income. These are the numbers your ownership group will care about most. Leasing Velocity and Vacancy Reduction AI leasing assistants handle prospect inquiries around the clock, schedule tours automatically, and follow up with leads that might otherwise go cold. The result is a measurable improvement in lead-to-lease conversion rates and a reduction in days on market per unit. How to calculate this impact: Find your current average days vacant per unit turn. Estimate the reduction in days vacant AI could deliver. Vendors typically cite 15–30% improvements, use conservative estimates. Multiply saved days by your average daily rent per unit. Multiply across your total annual unit turns. Example calculation: 200 units with an average of 2 turns per year = 400 turn events Current average days vacant: 18 days AI reduces vacancy by 20% = 3.6 fewer days per turn Average daily rent: $55 (based on $1,650/month) Value per turn: 3.6 × $55 = $198 Annual portfolio value: 400 × $198 = $79,200 This is a conservative, defensible number. Ownership groups respond well to conservative estimates because they signal intellectual honesty. Lead Conversion Rate Improvement If AI leasing tools capture and nurture leads that would otherwise go unanswered after hours, how much additional revenue does that represent? Work with your marketing team to identify your current lead-to-lease conversion rate, the volume of after-hours or unresponded inquiries, and the average lease value (monthly rent × average lease term in months). Even moving conversion by 2–3 percentage points across a portfolio of 500 units generates meaningful revenue. Rent Optimization AI-powered revenue management tools use real-time market data, competitor pricing, and demand signals to recommend optimal rent pricing. If your portfolio currently relies on manual comp analysis done weekly or monthly, you are likely leaving money on the table between reviews. To quantify this, ask your revenue management vendor for portfolio-specific modeling based on your submarket, unit mix, and current occupancy patterns. A 1–2% improvement in effective rent across a 500-unit portfolio at $1,650/month average rent adds roughly $165,000 to $330,000 in annualized revenue. Step 3: Quantify the Cost Savings The multifamily AI ROI business case is not just about revenue lift. Cost savings are equally important to ownership groups who manage tight expense ratios. Staff Time Reallocation This is one of the most underestimated line items in the AI ROI calculation. AI tools handle repetitive, time-consuming tasks: answering prospect FAQs, processing maintenance request triage, sending payment reminders, and generating routine reports. When those tasks are automated, your team's time shifts toward higher-value work. How to calculate this value: Identify the tasks your leasing, maintenance, and administrative staff spend the most repetitive time on. Estimate weekly hours consumed by those tasks. Multiply by hourly fully loaded labor cost (salary + benefits + overhead). Estimate the percentage of that time AI can realistically absorb. Even recovering 5 hours per week per leasing agent at a fully loaded cost of $28/hour saves $7,280 per agent per year. Important framing for ownership groups: Position this as reallocation, not elimination. You are not reducing headcount, you are enabling your existing team to focus on relationship-driven work that drives retention and satisfaction, which also has financial value. Maintenance Cost Reduction AI-powered maintenance tools use predictive analytics to flag equipment showing signs of early failure before a breakdown occurs. This shifts spending from expensive emergency repairs toward lower-cost preventive maintenance. Benchmark data commonly cited in proptech ROI studies suggests that predictive maintenance can reduce emergency repair costs by 10–25% and that equipment lifespan extensions of 15–20% are achievable with proactive servicing. Pull your prior two years of maintenance expense data. Identify your emergency/reactive repair spend as a percentage of total maintenance. Apply a conservative 10% reduction to that figure to estimate your savings. Turnover and Retention Impact Resident satisfaction is a financial metric. Every turnover event carries real costs like unit make-ready expenses, lost rent during vacancy, leasing commissions or marketing spend, and administrative time. AI tools that improve responsiveness, reduce maintenance delays, and create a better resident experience measurably reduce turnover rates. How to calculate this: Identify your current annual turnover rate. Estimate your all-in cost per turn (make-ready + vacancy loss + marketing). Apply a conservative 5–10% reduction in turnover as an AI impact estimate. Calculate the resulting savings. On a 300-unit portfolio with 50% annual turnover and a $3,500 all-in turn cost, reducing turnover by just 5% saves $26,250 per year. Administrative and Compliance Efficiency AI tools that assist with lead nurturing, lease generation, renewal workflows, and document management reduce the administrative burden on your team while lowering the risk of compliance errors. Though harder to quantify in dollar terms, the risk mitigation value is worth noting in your business case particularly for ownership groups who have faced lease compliance issues or fair housing concerns in the past. Step 4: Build the Business Case Document Once you have gathered and calculated your data, the presentation itself matters. Ownership groups respond to structure. Here is the recommended format for your multifamily AI ROI business case document. Section 1: Executive Summary Lead with the bottom line. State the three-year projected ROI as a percentage and in dollar terms. Include the payback period how many months until the investment breaks even. Keep this section to one page. Section 2: The Problem Statement Document the current-state pain points with data. What is your average vacancy duration? What is your lead response time after hours? What is your emergency maintenance spend? Quantified pain creates urgency. Section 3: The Proposed Solution Briefly describe the AI tool or suite you are recommending. Focus on what it does, not how it works technically. Connect each feature directly to one of the pain points in Section 2. Section 4: ROI Calculation Detail Present your full ROI model with clearly labeled assumptions. Show conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios. Ownership groups who see scenario modeling trust the presenter more because it signals that risks have been considered. Section 5: Implementation Timeline and Risk Mitigation Provide a realistic rollout timeline. Address the most common objections — staff disruption, data security, and integration complexity. Show that you have already vetted these concerns with your vendor. Section 6: Vendor Selection Rationale If you are recommending a specific platform, explain why. Include references from comparable operators, any pilot results, and contractual protections such as SLAs or performance guarantees. Step 5: Anticipate the Questions You Will Be Asked No budget approval meeting goes without hard questions. Prepare for these before you walk in. "What if the technology doesn't perform as promised?" Reference any pilot data, case studies from similar portfolio sizes or submarkets, and contractual performance guarantees. If a vendor is unwilling to commit to measurable outcomes in a contract, that is a red flag worth raising proactively. "What does this do to our team?" Be clear that the goal is augmentation, not replacement. Highlight the ways AI frees your team from low-value repetitive work and positions them for higher-impact resident relationship roles. If you anticipate staff resistance, address your change management plan briefly. "How does this compare to what competitors are doing?" If you have access to industry benchmarking data or know of competing properties in your submarket using AI tools, reference it. Framing AI adoption as a competitive necessity rather than a nice-to-have shifts the conversation meaningfully. "When will we see results?" Set realistic expectations. Leasing-side benefits like faster lead response and improved conversion can appear in 30–60 days. Maintenance savings and retention improvements typically take 6–12 months to show clearly in the data. The Metrics Ownership Groups Care About Most If you want your multifamily AI ROI business case to land, align your outputs to the metrics ownership groups already track: Net Operating Income (NOI): Show how revenue lift and cost savings flow directly to NOI. This is the language of asset management. Expense Ratio: Demonstrate how AI-driven efficiencies reduce operating expenses as a percentage of gross income. Days on Market / Vacancy Rate: Concrete, measurable, and directly tied to income. Cost Per Lead and Cost Per Lease: AI's impact on marketing efficiency is often significant and easy to track. Resident Retention Rate: Tie retention improvement to reduced turn costs and NOI stability. AI ROI for Property Management vs. Other Industries When you research AI ROI broadly, you will find frameworks built for enterprise software, manufacturing, or retail. Multifamily has its own dynamics. The ROI drivers here are shaped by lease cycles, resident lifecycle economics, maintenance seasonality, and labor market conditions specific to property management. Build your calculations using multifamily-specific benchmarks not generic proptech or SaaS ROI templates. Industry associations and proptech research firms publish multifamily-specific benchmarking data that can strengthen your assumptions. Where possible, use data from portfolios that match yours in unit count, asset class, and geographic market. How to Get Your First AI Pilot Approved If a full-portfolio rollout feels like too large a first ask, consider proposing a structured pilot. A single property or a subset of units allows you to generate real performance data from your own portfolio before committing to a broader investment. Structure the pilot with a defined time horizon (90 to 180 days is typical), agreed-upon success metrics established before the pilot begins, and a clear decision framework for what a successful pilot means in terms of full approval. Pilots reduce perceived risk for ownership groups while giving you the proof points to build an even stronger multifamily AI ROI business case for full deployment. Frequently Asked Questions What is a good ROI for AI in multifamily property management? A well-implemented AI platform should target a first-year ROI of 100–200%, with Year 2 and Year 3 returns climbing significantly higher once one-time implementation costs drop off. The exact figure depends on portfolio size, current operational inefficiencies, and which AI use cases you deploy. How long does it take to see ROI from multifamily AI? Leasing-side benefits such as faster lead response and improved conversion rates typically appear within 30–60 days. Maintenance cost savings and resident retention improvements usually require 6–12 months to show clearly in your data. What are the biggest cost savings from AI in property management? The most impactful cost savings come from staff time reallocation (automating repetitive tasks), reduced vacancy days through faster leasing, lower emergency maintenance costs via predictive analytics, and decreased resident turnover driven by improved satisfaction and responsiveness. How do I convince my ownership group to invest in AI? Build a data-backed business case that includes a full cost breakdown, conservative ROI projections across a three-year horizon, and scenario modeling with conservative, base, and optimistic estimates. Frame AI as a tool for improving NOI and expense ratios the metrics ownership groups already track. Should I start with a pilot or a full portfolio rollout? A structured pilot at a few properties is often the most effective first step. Define clear success metrics upfront, set a 30 to 60-day timeline, and establish in advance what results would justify a full-portfolio deployment. This approach lowers perceived risk while generating real proof points from your own portfolio. Bringing It All Together Building a credible multifamily AI ROI business case is not about selling technology. It is about speaking the language of asset performance, connecting operational improvements to financial outcomes, and presenting a picture of investment that is grounded in data your ownership group can verify. The operators who are winning budget approval for AI investment today are not doing so because AI is exciting. They are winning because they showed up to the meeting with conservative assumptions, clear calculations, and a realistic implementation plan that addressed the risks their ownership group cares about. That is the business case your ownership group is waiting to see.

title: Tax Diversification Helps Investors with Uncertainties of the Future
summary: Tax diversification is a strategy that encourages investors to be knowledgeable about the tax attributes of different accounts and intentional when funding these accounts.
body_text: Tax-Free Accounts Tax-free accounts are typically denoted by the word "Roth" in the title, like a Roth IRA or Roth 401(k). Tax-free accounts are funded with "after tax" dollars (like taxable accounts) which means a tax deduction is not provided when contributions are made. However, if the IRS rules are followed, all of the income and all of the gains in a tax-free account can be withdrawn in retirement totally free of income tax. In many cases, the owner of a tax-free Roth IRA account has more flexibility to withdraw contributions from the account before age 59 ½ without a penalty. Additionally, unlike tax-deferred accounts, tax-free Roth accounts do not force the account owner to take RMDs at a certain age. The IRS limits the amount that can be contributed per year to a tax-free account like a Roth 401(k) or Roth IRA. In some cases, a high earning individual may be prohibited from contributing directly to a Roth IRA. Tax Diversification Strategy The greatest benefit of funding different account types and being diversified from a tax standpoint is flexibility. It is impossible to guarantee what the tax brackets, RMD rules, and capital gains tax rates will be at any point in the future. Having tax diversified accounts will allow a retiree to use their capital in the most tax efficient manner regardless of how the rules change. Tax diversification also encourages investors to be mindful when funding retirement accounts. In high income years when a worker is subject to higher tax rates it may make more sense to fund tax deferred accounts to get a current tax deduction. In lower income years when a tax deduction isn't as useful, funding tax-free accounts may be the ideal long-term solution. It is important for investors to be educated on all available options and thoughtfully prepare a financial plan. Competent advice from a qualified tax advisor or CPA is also critically important.
